step1_analysis.circuit_type: Common-Source Amplifier with Cascode Active Load
step1_analysis.description: A single-ended common-source amplifier (NMOS) with a PMOS cascode active load. It is likely a single branch of a high-gain operational amplifier (e.g., folded-cascode or telescopic) used in the MDAC stages of the pipeline ADC.

paper_reference.title: A Cost-Efficient High-Speed 12-bit Pipeline ADC in 0.18-m Digital CMOS

dc_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the amplifier, critical for minimizing finite gain error in pipeline stages.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm3 * (ro3 || (gm2*ro2*ro1)). With VDD=1.8V, Vbias1=1.0V, Id~36uA. gm3~450uS, ro3~277kOhm. Since the NMOS is not cascoded, Rout is dominated by ro3. Gain ~ gm3*ro3 = 124 V/V = 41.8 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The NMOS is not cascoded, so the output resistance is dominated by ro3, limiting the gain of this specific branch to around 40-50 dB.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency where the voltage gain drops to 0 dB, determining the settling time of the amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: UGF = gm3 / (2*pi*CL). With gm3=450uS and CL=100fF, UGF = 716 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A UGF of ~700 MHz provides a time constant of ~0.22 ns, which is fast enough to settle within the 4.5 ns half-period required for 110 MS/s operation.

phase_margin.description: Phase difference from instability at the unity gain frequency, ensuring stable closed-loop operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominant pole at output (5.7 MHz), non-dominant pole at cascode node N1 (3 GHz). Phase shift at 716 MHz is ~103 degrees. PM = 180 - 103 = 77 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The non-dominant pole at the cascode node is at a much higher frequency than the UGF, resulting in a healthy phase margin > 60 degrees.

power_consumption.description: Static power dissipated by this amplifier branch.

sky130_expected.calculation: Power = VDD * Id. With VDD=1.8V and Id=36uA, Power = 64.8 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: This is just a single branch of an op-amp. The total ADC power is 97 mW, so a single branch consuming ~65 uW is highly realistic.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC gain, UGF, phase margin, and power consumption using an AC-coupled input with a massive inductor in DC feedback to perfectly bias the amplifier in its high-gain region.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Cascode Amplifier Branch
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u

XM1 N1 LABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 LABEL_NET_2 N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N0 LABEL_NET_3 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VGND GND 0 0

* Supply connections
V_LABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 1.8
V_N2 N2 0 0

* Bias voltages for PMOS cascode
V_LABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 1.0
V_LABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 0.5

* Input signal with DC feedback for self-biasing in high-gain region
Vac IN_AC 0 dc 0 ac 1
C1 IN_AC LABEL_NET_3 1
L1 N0 LABEL_NET_3 1G

* Load capacitance
CL N0 0 100f

.control
op
let power = -i(V_LABEL_NET_0) * 1.8
print power
print v(N0)

ac dec 100 1 10G
let gain_db = vdb(N0)
let phase = 180/PI * cph(v(N0))
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=10
meas ac ugf when gain_db=0 fall=1
meas ac phase_at_ugf find phase when gain_db=0 fall=1
quit
.endc
.end
